record_type_quote: Considering the existing findings of ASB meta-analysis of European populations (Karlsson Linnér et al., 2021) and absent GWAS data for individuals from Russia, the present study aimed to evaluate the applicability of calculated polygenic scores based on existing GWAS data to predict severe ASB (homicide) in the Russian cohort.

targets.title: Multivariate analysis of 1.5 million people identifies genetic associations with traits related to self-regulation and addiction.
targets.evidence_quote: Considering the existing findings of ASB meta-analysis of European populations (Karlsson Linnér et al., 2021) and absent GWAS data for individuals from Russia, the present study aimed to evaluate the applicability of calculated polygenic scores based on existing GWAS data to predict severe ASB (homicide) in the Russian cohort.
targets.outcome_quote: Since no significant difference in predicting ASB risk in the VUR sample was observed among models based on “weighted” and “unweighted” effects of SNPs, it can be concluded that effect estimates from GWAS of Europeans seem to be inappropriate for individuals from Russia.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly judge the original European effect estimates inappropriate for the Russian cohort, the transferability claim retested here. PGS still explains a small proportion of variance; this makes the verdict less certain but does not override their negative assessment of the transferred estimates.

reasoning: Tests transfer of specific published GWAS effect estimates in independent homicide and control samples. The 2021 GWAS is the explicit source and retested predictive result. Other cited studies provide context and comparisons, not independently designed replications. Title and authors verified.
